Essentially, df is for an overview, while du is for granularity. If a mnemonic helps, then maybe use "dug" for "du = granularity" and also to imply that one digs into the filesystem when using it?

I primarily just use df for df -h, whereas I'll use du for du -sh * | sort -h | tail -5

I use df -h similarly. Sometimes I'll give it a directory or simply . to specify just one filesystem for output simplicity. My favorite du one-liner for finding disk-filling culprits: du | sort -nr | head -n50

It will show you the files/directories using the most space under your current working directory. Like df you can also give it a particular directory to show, but I'm usually already in the directory I want to check so I can rm or xz stuff.
